The petitioners, thereafter, filed an application before the 1st Court of Settlement, Dhaka on 16-7-2000 for exclusion of the house from 'Kha' list but the Court of Settlement returned the petition to the petitioners by an order dated 17-12-2000 holding that the limitation of 108 days for filing an application under section 7(1) of the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance, 1985 for exclusion of a house from the list of Abandoned Buildings had expired on 8-1-1987 and the court had no jurisdiction to entertain an application barred by 13 years, Annexure F. 

 35. In this case, the question arose as to whether the Writ Petition is maintainable in view of the fact that the Court of Settlement has rejected her case on ground of limitation. Similar questions arose in the cases of Saleha Begum vs Chairman, 1st Court of Settlement and another, reported in 49 DLR 243 and in the case of Rehana Kamal and another vs Chairman, Court of Settlement and others, reported in 3 BLC 213 and the concurrent findings of this court, in this regard, is: 

 "Although the petitioner's application was rejected by the Court of Settlement on the ground of limitation but the High Court Division has ample power, while exercising the powers under Writ Jurisdiction, to look into the factual aspect where fundamental rights of the petitioners have been violated as guaranteed under Article 42 of the Constitution."
